s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic scrotal swelling with acute worsening and a palpable testicular mass
salient_findings: Firm, smooth testis without discrete nodules or tenderness
Well-circumscribed hypoechoic lesion in the left testis with internal blood flow on ultrasound
key_facts: 49-year-old man
Left testicular bloating and dull pain for 20 years
Acute worsening of symptoms over the past 10 days
No other medical history
Left testis was enlarged, firm, and smooth on examination
Transillumination was negative
Scrotal Doppler ultrasound showed bilateral epididymal cysts
A 1.09 × 0.79 cm well-circumscribed hypoechoic lesion in the left testis with internal blood flow
Small left hydrocele
Elevated serum CA19-9 level of 57.5 U/mL
Normal alpha-fetoprotein, human chorionic gonadotropin, and other tumor markers

raw.syndrome_frame: Chronic scrotal swelling with acute worsening and a palpable testicular mass
salient_findings: Firm, smooth testis without discrete nodules or tenderness
Well-circumscribed hypoechoic lesion in the left testis with internal blood flow on ultrasound
key_facts: 49-year-old man
Left testicular bloating and dull pain for 20 years
Acute worsening of symptoms over the past 10 days
No other medical history
Left testis was enlarged, firm, and smooth on examination
Transillumination was negative
Scrotal Doppler ultrasound showed bilateral epididymal cysts
A 1.09 × 0.79 cm well-circumscribed hypoechoic lesion in the left testis with internal blood flow
Small left hydrocele
Elevated serum CA19-9 level of 57.5 U/mL
Normal alpha-fetoprotein, human chorionic gonadotropin, and other tumor markers

differentials: Malignant fibrous histiocytoma of the testis
Malignant fibrous histiocytoma of the testis

shortlist.label: Seminoma
shortlist.why_kept: Most common testicular cancer, matches palpable testicular mass and acute worsening

shortlist.label: Non-seminomatous germ cell tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Common testicular cancer, consistent with elevated CA19-9 and palpable mass

shortlist.label: Testicular lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Possible cause of testicular swelling and acute worsening, especially in older adults

shortlist.label: Leydig cell tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Can cause testicular enlargement and hormone elevation, consistent with some case findings

shortlist.label: Embryonal carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Aggressive testicular cancer, possible cause of rapid worsening and elevated tumor markers

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of a long-standing, slowly enlarging testicular mass with recent acute worsening, along with the ultrasound findings of a well-circumscribed hypoechoic lesion and the laboratory result of an elevated CA19-9 level, is most consistent with a Leydig cell tumor. Leydig cell tumors can produce various substances leading to hormonal imbalances and can have elevated tumor markers such as CA19-9.

rejected.label: Seminoma
rejected.why: Seminomas typically present with more rapid growth and often have elevated human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG) levels, which is not the case here.

rejected.label: Non-seminomatous germ cell tumor
rejected.why: These tumors usually have a more complex appearance on ultrasound and often have elevated alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) levels, which is not seen in this patient.

rejected.label: Testicular lymphoma
rejected.why: Lymphomas of the testis are more common in older men and typically present with more systemic symptoms and rapid progression, not consistent with this patient's 20-year history of symptoms.

rejected.label: Embryonal carcinoma
rejected.why: Embryonal carcinomas are aggressive tumors that often present with metastatic disease at diagnosis and have elevated AFP levels, which does not match this patient's presentation or laboratory findings.
